results.result: Cell-to-cell transmission of HIV-1 from SUPT1 cells to THP-1 cells induces inflammasome activation in a manner dependent on cell-to-cell contact. SUPT1 cells lack a functional CARD8 inflammasome pathway, allowing attribution of inflammasome outputs to THP-1 cells. Transwell experiments preventing cell-to-cell contact abolished IL-1β secretion despite equivalent viral titers.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C28 are well-supported by experimental data in Figure 1. The VbP control (C25) validates that SUPT1 cells lack CARD8 function, the coculture data (C26) shows HIV-dependent IL-1β secretion, and the transwell experiment (C27) demonstrates cell-to-cell contact dependence. The inference (C28) logically follows from the data.

results.result: CARD8 is the primary sensor driving inflammasome activation during HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission to THP-1 cells, with minimal contribution from NLRP3. CARD8 KO THP-1 cells showed no IL-1β secretion upon HIV-1 coculture, while the NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 had only modest effects. VX765 (CASP1 inhibitor) and lopinavir (HIVPR inhibitor) completely blocked IL-1β secretion.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C34 are supported by Figure 2 data showing CARD8 KO abolishes IL-1β secretion while MCC950 has minimal effect. The controls with nigericin (C32) validate inhibitor function. The conclusion that CARD8 is the primary sensor (C30, C34) is well-supported by the differential effects of genetic and pharmacological perturbations.

results.result: HIV-dependent inflammasome activation occurs in primary MDMs during cell-to-cell infection in a manner dependent on viral entry, HIVPR, and CASP1, but independent of NLRP3. Only CCR5-tropic HIV-1NL4.3-BaL (not CXCR4-tropic HIV-1LAI) induced IL-1β secretion. Lopinavir and VX765 blocked IL-1β secretion, while nevirapine (RT inhibitor) and MCC950 (NLRP3 inhibitor) had no effect.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C41 are well-supported by Figure 3A data showing viral tropism dependence and differential inhibitor effects. The use of multiple inhibitors targeting different stages (entry, protease, RT, CASP1, NLRP3) provides strong evidence for the proposed mechanism. The inference that incoming HIVPR is sufficient (C39) is supported by NVP persistence.

results.result: Inflammasome activation in MDMs following HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission is detectable by 24 hours and persists through 72 hours. IL-1β secretion is unaffected by nevirapine treatment, indicating that incoming HIVPR (rather than de novo synthesized protease) is responsible for CARD8 activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C44 are supported by Figure 3B time-course data showing IL-1β detection by 24h and persistence with NVP treatment. The inference that CARD8 is the likely sensor (C44) is reasonable given the combined evidence of HIVPR dependence, RT independence, and NLRP3 independence, though direct genetic evidence in MDMs is provided separately.

results.result: CARD8 is required for inflammasome activation in primary MDMs during HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission. CARD8 KO MDMs from five donors showed marked reduction in CARD8 protein and significant reduction in IL-1β secretion upon HIV-1 coculture. NLRP3 KO had no effect on inflammasome activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C48 are strongly supported by Figure 3C-D showing CARD8 KO efficiency by immunoblot and genetic analysis, and consistent reduction in IL-1β across all five donors. The NLRP3 KO control (C47) further supports CARD8 as the primary sensor. The conclusion (C48) is well-justified by the genetic evidence.

results.result: Cell-to-cell transmission of HIV-1 from primary CD4+ T cells to primary MDMs induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation driven by HIVPR and CASP1. Inflammasome activation persists in the presence of nevirapine and is detectable by 24 hours, with lopinavir completely blocking IL-1β secretion.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C52 are supported by Figure 4A-B showing HIV-dependent IL-1β secretion blocked by LPV and VX765 but not NVP. The time-course data (C52) confirms 24h detection. This extends the SUPT1:MDM findings to a fully primary cell system, strengthening the physiological relevance of the observations.

results.result: CARD8 is required for inflammasome activation in MDMs during HIV-1 transmission from primary CD4+ T cells. CARD8 KO MDMs showed significant decrease in IL-1β secretion compared to AAVS1 KO controls when cocultured with HIV-infected primary CD4+ T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C55 are supported by Figure 4C-D showing CARD8 KO efficiency and reduced IL-1β secretion in CARD8 KO MDMs. This provides genetic evidence for CARD8 requirement in a fully primary cell system, complementing the SUPT1:MDM data and strengthening the conclusion that CARD8 plays a pivotal role.

results.result: Protease inhibitor-resistant (PI-R) HIV-1 strains differentially cleave CARD8 compared to wildtype HIV-1LAI. Some PI-R clones (PI-R2, PI-R3, PI-R5, PI-R9, PI-R10) showed reduced CARD8 cleavage, while others (PI-R12, PI-R13) showed enhanced cleavage. All PI-R strains maintained similar levels of viral Gag polyprotein processing.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C60 are supported by Figure 5A showing differential CARD8 cleavage by PI-R strains while maintaining similar p24/p55 ratios. The quantification of CARD8 cleavage products provides clear evidence for differential host protein targeting. The conclusion that naturally occurring mutations affect CARD8 (C60) is well-supported.

results.result: PI-R strains that differentially cleave CARD8 also induce corresponding differences in inflammasome activation. PI-R2 and PI-R9 (reduced CARD8 cleavage) induced lower IL-1β levels, while PI-R12 and PI-R13 (enhanced CARD8 cleavage) induced higher IL-1β levels compared to HIV-1LAI in both reconstituted and cell-to-cell transmission assays.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C64 are supported by Figure 5B-C showing consistent correlation between CARD8 cleavage efficiency and IL-1β secretion across three experimental systems. The consistency across biochemical, reconstituted, and cell-to-cell assays provides strong evidence that protease mutations affect inflammasome activation through altered CARD8 cleavage.

results.result: Cell-to-cell transmission of HIV-1 from T cells to myeloid cells yields CARD8-dependent, NLRP3-independent inflammasome activation via incoming HIVPR in both immortalized and primary cell models. PI-R mutations affect the ability of HIVPR to cleave host proteins including CARD8.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C67 summarize the major findings supported by data throughout the manuscript. The CARD8 dependence is shown in multiple systems (THP-1, MDMs, primary CD4:MDM), NLRP3 independence is demonstrated by MCC950 and NLRP3 KO experiments, and PI-R effects are shown in Figure 5. These summary claims accurately reflect the experimental evidence.

results.result: HIV-dependent CARD8 inflammasome activation during cell-free infection requires DEAE-dextran, which may increase viral dose entering cells. DEAE-dextran can trigger inflammasome activation in some THP-1 cell lines. A considerable influx of incoming HIVPR may be necessary for CARD8 activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C78 and C81 are supported by data referenced in Appendix 1. However, C79 and C80 are explicitly speculative hypotheses proposed by the authors to explain the DEAE-dextran requirement. While the speculation is reasonable, these mechanistic claims lack direct experimental validation. The result is supported as stated but contains speculative elements.

results.result: Inflammasome activation following cell-to-cell transmission is detectable by 24 hours (delayed compared to 2-hour detection in cell-free infection with DEAE-dextran). IL-1β levels plateau after 24 hours, suggesting secondary infection does not further amplify inflammasome activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C84 are supported by Figures 3B and 4B showing IL-1β detection at 24h and plateau thereafter. The inference that secondary infection does not amplify activation (C84) is reasonable given the plateau, though alternative explanations (e.g., cytokine consumption, cell death) are not fully excluded. The comparison to cell-free infection timing is appropriate.

results.result: The authors speculate that differential CARD8 activation by PI-R strains could influence HIV-1 disease progression, that CARD8 may influence viral variant selection during protease inhibitor therapy, and that CARD8 activation could drive HIV-1 pathogenesis through chronic immune activation and indirect promotion of CD4+ T cell depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C76, C77, C85, C86, C90, and C92 are explicitly speculative and lack direct experimental support in this manuscript. While the speculation is reasonable given the demonstrated differential CARD8 activation by PI-R strains and the known relationship between inflammation and disease progression (C75), these claims represent hypotheses for future investigation rather than supported conclusions.

results.result: CARD8 detects HIV-1 infection by sensing incoming HIVPR activity through a substrate mimic motif in its N-terminus. HIVPR cleavage of CARD8 occurs rapidly after infection and can be prevented by HIVPR and fusion inhibitors but not RT inhibitors, indicating detection of virion-packaged protease.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C13-C17 describe prior work establishing the CARD8-HIVPR sensing mechanism. These are well-supported by multiple citations to prior research including the authors' own work. While not new findings in this manuscript, they provide essential context and are accurately represented.

results.result: Background claims about HIV-1 pathogenesis, cellular targets, inflammasome biology, cell-to-cell transmission mechanisms, and CARD8 function in T cells are established by prior research and provide context for the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C24 represent established knowledge supported by appropriate citations to prior research. These background claims are accurately stated and provide necessary context. C19 involves inference from C18 but is reasonable given that IL-1β/IL-18 are key inflammatory mediators.

results.result: Prior research implicated NLRP3 and IFI16 in HIV-1 sensing, but recent work shows CARD8 is required for pyroptosis in CD4+ T cells and is a major driver of T cell depletion. CARD8 is also the primary sensor in myeloid cells. Macrophages, unlike T cells, release IL-1β in response to HIV-1 and may be a source of chronic inflammation. Inflammation predicts disease progression better than viral load.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C93 (excluding speculative claims already grouped) represent a mix of prior knowledge (C68-C75, C87, C93) and integration of current findings with prior work (C74, C88-C89, C91). All are supported by appropriate citations or data. C73 and C89 involve reasonable inferences from the cited/presented evidence about CARD8's role in pathogenesis.

results.result: Cell-to-cell transmission of HIV-1 between infected T cells and THP-1 cells induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation that is largely independent of NLRP3. This was demonstrated using coculture systems showing IL-1β secretion dependent on cell-to-cell contact, with CARD8 KO but not NLRP3 inhibition blocking the response.
results.evaluation: Both reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. Reviewer 1 states 'The data convincingly support the idea that CARD8 is activated by the viral protease, promoting inflammation.' Reviewer 2 notes 'Co-cultures of HIV-infected T cells with macrophages led to viral spreading, resulting in IL1β release and cell death, with CARD8 playing a crucial role in this inflammasome response.'

results.result: Cell-to-cell transmission of HIV-1 from infected T cells to primary monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation via incoming HIVPR that is largely NLRP3-independent. This was demonstrated across multiple donors using CARD8 KO MDMs, showing dependence on viral protease and CASP1 but not reverse transcriptase or NLRP3.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding. Reviewer 1 notes 'The study's significance is further enhanced by including time-course analyses in primary T cells and macrophages.' Reviewer 2 states 'The authors have addressed initial weaknesses and verified effects in cocultures of primary T cells and macrophages. They now also provide evidence that CARD8 is activated by protease from incoming viral particles.'

results.result: HIV-1 transmission from primary CD4+ T cells to primary MDMs induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation driven by incoming HIVPR and CASP1. This was demonstrated using infected primary CD4+ T cells cocultured with CARD8 KO versus control MDMs, showing significant reduction in IL-1β secretion in CARD8 KO cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this primary cell validation. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The authors have addressed initial weaknesses and verified effects in cocultures of primary T cells and macrophages,' indicating acceptance of these findings as addressing prior concerns about the use of primary cells.

results.result: HIV-1 protease inhibitor-resistant (PI-R) mutants differentially cleave and activate CARD8 compared to wildtype HIV-1. Some PI-R clones showed reduced CARD8 cleavage and IL-1β production (PI-R2, PI-R9), while others showed enhanced activity (PI-R12, PI-R13), despite similar viral polyprotein processing activity. This indicates that naturally occurring protease mutations can modulate host innate immune responses.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognize the clinical relevance of this finding. Reviewer 2 states 'The authors also found that HIV isolates resistant to protease inhibitors showed differences in CARD8 activation and IL1β production, highlighting the clinical relevance of their findings,' indicating acceptance of this result as a significant contribution.

results.result: CARD8 is the primary innate sensor during HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission in myeloid cells, with macrophages releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines in response to incoming HIVPR. This occurs in a largely NLRP3-independent manner and represents a potential source of sustained IL-1β and chronic immune activation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this overarching conclusion. Reviewer 2 states 'Overall, this well-written study provides strong evidence for the role of CARD8 in protease-dependent sensing of viral spread, with implications for understanding chronic inflammation in HIV infections and its potential contribution to systemic immune activation.'

results.result: Differential CARD8 inflammasome activation by protease variants could influence disease progression in people living with HIV harboring HIVPR resistance mutations, and may affect viral variant selection during protease inhibitor therapy. IL-1β release from macrophages may contribute to pathogenesis by activating CD4+ T cells and promoting chronic immune activation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge these as speculative implications requiring further study. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'Further studies are needed to clarify how much this mechanism contributes to systemic immune activation in untreated infections and whether this mechanism drives chronic inflammation under ART,' indicating these claims are not yet fully supported by the current data.

results.result: Cell-free HIV-1 infection requires DEAE-dextran to induce CARD8 inflammasome activation, suggesting that a considerable influx of incoming HIVPR is necessary for activation. Cell-to-cell transmission achieves this threshold without cationic polymer, with IL-1β levels plateauing by 24 hours, suggesting secondary infection does not further amplify the response.
results.evaluation: While reviewers do not explicitly discuss these mechanistic details, they accept the overall evidence for incoming protease activation. Reviewer 2 states 'They now also provide evidence that CARD8 is activated by protease from incoming viral particles,' which encompasses these supporting mechanistic observations.

results.result: CARD8 detects HIV-1 infection by sensing incoming HIV protease activity through a substrate mimic motif in its N-terminus, which functions as a molecular tripwire. This occurs rapidly after infection and can be prevented by protease and fusion inhibitors but not reverse transcriptase inhibitors.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these background claims from prior work. Reviewer 2 notes 'Following up on their previous work, the authors investigated whether HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission activates the CARD8 inflammasome,' indicating acceptance of the established CARD8 sensing mechanism as the foundation for the current study.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims C1, C2, C13-C17 establishing prior CARD8-HIVPR sensing mechanism. Both recognize these as foundational context from prior work that is accurately represented.

Strong agreement on speculative nature of claims C76, C77, C90, C92. Both evaluations classify these as UNCERTAIN/speculative, requiring further study to establish connections between CARD8 activation and clinical outcomes in HIV infection.

Both support claims C26-C28 regarding HIV-dependent IL-1β secretion in coculture and cell-to-cell contact dependence. OpenEval also includes C25 (VbP control validation). Peer review groups these with additional CARD8 mechanism claims (C29, C30, C33, C34).

Both support CARD8 as primary sensor (C29, C30, C33, C34). OpenEval separately evaluates these claims with Figure 2 data, while peer review groups them with coculture findings as part of overall CARD8 activation evidence.

Strong agreement on viral tropism and inhibitor data (C35-C41). Both recognize this as evidence for incoming HIVPR sufficiency. Peer review groups these with additional primary cell validation claims (C42-C48).
Both support time-course data showing IL-1β detection by 24h (C42-C44). OpenEval evaluates separately, while peer review groups with broader primary cell evidence including CARD8 KO data.
Both support CARD8 KO efficiency and IL-1β reduction in MDMs (C45-C48). OpenEval emphasizes genetic evidence across five donors, while peer review groups with incoming protease activation evidence.
Strong agreement on primary CD4:MDM coculture data (C49-C52) showing HIV-dependent IL-1β secretion with appropriate inhibitor controls. Both recognize this as validation in fully primary cell system.
Both support CARD8 KO in primary MDMs (C53-C55) as genetic validation. OpenEval evaluates separately, while peer review groups with CD4:MDM coculture data as part of primary cell validation.
Strong agreement on differential CARD8 cleavage by PI-R strains (C56-C60). Both recognize clinical relevance of naturally occurring protease mutations affecting CARD8 activation.

Both support correlation between CARD8 cleavage and IL-1β secretion across systems (C61-C64). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across three experimental approaches, while peer review groups with PI-R strain data (C56-C60, C67).

Both support major summary findings (C65-C66) regarding CARD8 dependence and NLRP3 independence. OpenEval includes C67 (PI-R effects), while peer review groups with broader implications for HIV pathogenesis (C74, C88, C89, C91).

Both support DEAE-dextran requirement data (C78, C81). OpenEval notes C79-C80 are speculative mechanistic hypotheses, while peer review accepts overall incoming protease evidence without explicitly discussing these mechanistic details.

Both support 24h IL-1β detection timing (C82-C84). OpenEval evaluates separately with inference about secondary infection, while peer review groups with broader incoming protease mechanism (C78-C81, C85-C86).

Both support integration of findings with prior knowledge about CARD8's role in pathogenesis (C74, C88, C89, C91). OpenEval groups broader background claims (C68-C93 excluding speculative), while peer review focuses on overarching conclusions.

OpenEval separately evaluates background claims C7-C24 (inflammasome biology, HIV pathogenesis context) as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found; these are implicitly accepted as background.
